reasons: The two answers are almost word-for-word the same. Both open by correcting both premises: Henan hukou holders can get a replacement card in Guangzhou, and the 12306 electronic temporary ID gives 24-hour validity, 6 uses a month, with the station window as a fallback. Both give the right fees (40 yuan replacement, 10 yuan temporary ID, 3-month validity), both carry over the unverified '40-day official' limit and the 'paper certificate is free' trap, and neither mentions the 60-day statutory limit. B wins narrowly because it derives its dates from stated assumptions, and its arithmetic checks out: 40 days from Oct 23 is about Dec 2, and 5 working days lands around Oct 30. A instead adds unverifiable 'usually 3-4 weeks', 'about a week' and '上千元' figures, and its '3-4 weeks' does not match its own 'late Nov to early Dec'.
